sheet.name: Name

dodge.name: Dodge
dodge.description: Dodge is your skill at getting out of the way of bullets, energy beams, knives and punches. It is used extensively in personal combat and determines your Defence (Dodge) bonus.

energyWeapons.name: Energy Weapons
energyWeapons.description: Energy Weapons cover all laser and beam weapons used in personal combat, except for those which are shoulder or tripod mounted. The higher your energy weapons Skill the more likely you are to hit and the more damage burst weapons, such as the Assault Beamer, will inflict.

fighting.name: Fighting
fighting.description: Fighting is the skill that governs weaponless combat, such as boxing, wrestling, kung fu, headbutting and any other noble martial art. Fighting can include improvised weapons such as chair legs and broken bottles, but any close combat weapon designed for combat falls under the Melee Weapons Skill. Fighting can be a useful skill for taking opponents alive as the damage it inflicts is (generally) non-lethal.

grenade.name: Grenade
grenade.description: This Skill allows you to use grenades with a semblance of accuracy and safety. It also covers the ability to use and disarm explosives of all kinds.

heavyWeapons.name: Heavy Weapons
heavyWeapons.description: Heavy Weapons are large tripod or shoulder mounted weapons used in Personal Combat such as chain guns, missile launchers and plasma cannons. Heavy Weapons are powerful, but difficult to use and aim in small scale, fast moving skirmishes. This Skill can also be used to fire weapons mounted on vehicles provided that you are personally operating the weapon. If you are relying on the vehicle’s targeting computer you must use the Vehicle Weapons Skill.

kineticWeapons.name: Kinetic Weapons
kineticWeapons.description: Kinetic Weapons cover all projectile based weapons used in personal combat such as autopistols, assault rifles and shotguns. Weapons which are shoulder or tripod mounted use the Heavy Weapons Skill instead. The higher your Kinetic Weapons Skill the more likely you are to hit and the more damage burst weapons will inflict.

meleeWeapons.name: Melee Weapons
meleeWeapons.description: The Melee Weapons Skill covers the use of all close combat weapons such as swords, clubs, and axes as well as more exotic close range weapons such as Cyberclaws. Melee Weapons are rarely used by common folk but are beloved of assassins and expert mercenaries who like to kill cleanly and silently.

parry.name: Parry
parry.description: The Parry Skill is used to deflect close combat attacks, both from Melee Weapons and from fighting. It is very useful as it allows a chance to counter-attack against opponent that misses you. See the chapter on Personal Combat for details.

computer.name: Computer
computer.description: Computers are easy to use in the 34th century, but quite hard to crack. The Computer Skill allows you to hack terminals, interrogate secured databases and even to reprogram the computer’s basic functions.

cultureLaw.name: Culture & Law
cultureLaw.description: Culture and Law is your knowledge of interstellar society including its rules, history, art forms, codes of conduct and its important leaders. Educated people are expected to know about these kinds of things, whilst the unwashed masses, in their ignorance, might know only their local planet’s customs and nothing else.

cyber.name: Cyber
cyber.description: The Cyber Skill allows you to repair and modify robots, drones and cybernetic attachments. It also covers your skill in remotely piloting any drones you might own or be currently in control of.

medicine.name: Medicine
medicine.description: The Medicine Skill covers everything from patching up wounds to resuscitating a dying comrade. Characters with the Trained Doctor background can even attempt surgery, but should refrain from doing anything too ambitious until they get a good Skill level. Medicine can also be used to diagnose medical problems such as disease, poisoning and chemical intoxication. Provided suitable medical facilities are available most of these problems, once diagnosed, can be cured within a day or so.

planetaryKnowledge.name: Planetary Knowledge
planetaryKnowledge.description: This Skill represents your knowledge of different planets – their general location, their systems of government, and their general economy. Although most people rely on computers to give them facts about other worlds, restrictive modern copyright law means most interstellar encyclopedias are shockingly incomplete. Well-known systems such as Sol or Achenar are easy to recall, whereas obscure outer rim worlds are more difficult. This Skill ties in nicely with Navigation. Navigation tells you how to get to a new system; Planetary Knowledge tells you what is actually there.

science.name: Science
science.description: The Science Skill includes the three great sciences, physics, chemistry and biology. Science lets you understand how things work in the universe and can be used to predict the effects of an action. On a practical level you can use Science to understand how close you can fly to a turbulent planet or star, to calculate if your ship will still be able to take off on a heavy gravity world, or to estimate when that supernova is going to go critical. A good knowledge of science makes you look very smart, which can be helpful in some situations.

tactics.name: Tactics
tactics.description: Tactics is your ability to assess a situation quickly and determine the best course of action. It is mostly used to determine initiative in Combat, but it can also be used to spot good ambush areas or to predict the actions of an enemy commander on the battlefield.

trading.name: Trading
trading.description: Trading is the ability to understand and prosper in the complex trading environment of the Elite: Dangerous universe. This Skill is mostly used between adventures to gather extra income – a good Trading Skill and a large cargo hold can net a large amount of extra cash. You will use it in game to predict good trading routes and to judge whether the sale price of an item is fair or not.

bargain.name: Bargain
bargain.description: Bargain is your skill in getting what you want in some kind of exchange, usually involving money. You can use it with vendors and shop keepers to get cheaper equipment, and it can also be used to bribe people. The GM might allow you to use this Skill between adventures to get cheaper equipment.

bluff.name: Bluff
bluff.description: Bluff is your skill at lying, deception and disguise. Use it to convince people you are someone you are not or to play the innocent when the police turn up.

charm.name: Charm
charm.description: Charm is your ability to make people feel good about themselves and to trust you based on nothing more than your raw charisma. People who like you are less inclined to be suspicious of you or to want to harm you. It works well with other abilities such as Diplomacy, Bluff and Bargain.

diplomacy.name: Diplomacy
diplomacy.description: Diplomacy is the ability to resolve disputes through respect and persuasion, treating your debating target as an equal. Use it when you wish to show common cause with a potential enemy, or to explain, rationally, what you are doing, to a suspicious guard. Diplomacy relies on openness and honesty – if you are lying to your target use Bluff instead.

gambling.name: Gambling
gambling.description: With Gambling you increase your skill in all games of chance, from card games to token slot machines. You can count cards and figure out the win/loss conditions programmed into casino gambling machines.

insight.name: Insight
insight.description: The Insight Skill allows you to read people’s emotional state by studying their faces and body posture. It is not telepathy but it can tell you if a person is lying, earnest, angry, in love or intoxicated, making it very helpful during interrogations and questioning.

intimidate.name: Intimidate
intimidate.description: Intimidate lets you cajole, threaten and bully obedience into a person. It is a very aggressive form of communication but is sometimes the best way to shock an angry foe into submission.

streetwise.name: Streetwise
streetwise.description: Surviving in rough urban areas when you are a nice, middle class spaceship owner can be tough. Many street gangs use a vernacular that is hard to understand and follow a set of cultural mores that might not be consistent with society in general. In order to find information or discover where to buy rare, possibly illegal, items, you’ll need Streetwise to navigate your way through the shocking criminal underclass of the galaxy.

navigation.name: Navigation
navigation.description: Navigation covers all forms of orienteering, map reading and astro-navigation. You can plot a route through mountain ranges or nebula, figure out where you are if you become lost, and work out the most efficient routes in all kinds of terrain. Most Navigation is done with the aid of computers in the 34th century, but you are also able to navigate using stars and by identifying major landscape locations provided you have some knowledge of the planet you are on

repair.name: Repair
repair.description: Your Repair Skill allows you to fix all kinds of machinery, including spaceships and vehicles. While most pieces of technology have readable ‘fix-it’ guides downloadable from a chip inside the device or machine, Repair shows how handy you are around machines. It measures your skill and dexterity at using tools and the common sense required not to mess up the job and make things worse

shipPiloting.name: Spaceship Piloting
shipPiloting.description: This is your skill at flying spaceships. In addition to being used when you make any dangerous manoeuvres, such as skimming asteroids or flying down narrow canyons, it is primarily used in Spaceship Combat to determine the Defence of your ship.

shipWeapons.name: Spaceship Weapons
shipWeapons.description: Governs your ability to hit with weapons mounted on spaceships. This is used in Spaceship Combat.

systems.name: Systems
systems.description: This Skill allows you to operate scanner and sensor systems on a spaceship or ground based vehicle. It also allows you to activate and control the internal machinery inside a spaceship or vehicle, such as the airlocks and bulkheads, or any mining equipment like refineries or drones. Normally things like adjusting the temperature don’t require a Skill check, but sucking the air out of a passenger compartment or overloading the engines to explode might.

vehiclePiloting.name: Vehicle Piloting
vehiclePiloting.description: This is your ability to drive or pilot ground or underwater vehicles such as SRV’s or Subs. It is mostly used to determine your Defence in Vehicle Combat, but is also used when you try to pull off a very difficult manoeuvre such as performing a sharp turn or driving over a high ramp.

vehicleWeapons.name: Vehicle Weapons
vehicleWeapons.description: Governs your ability to hit with weapons mounted on vehicles. This is used in Vehicle Combat.

athletics.name: Athletics
athletics.description: Athletics represents your ability to jump, run, climb, swim and otherwise perform feats of physical prowess. It is also used to see how long you can hold your breath and how far you can run.

perception.name: Perception
perception.description: Perception covers the use of all five senses, sight, sound, touch, taste and smell. It is used to spot hidden items, detect ambushes, listen through closed doors and to identify a strange taste or smell. Spies and paranoid soldiers rely on a good perception to spot potential trouble before it strikes.

security.name: Security
security.description: Security is your understanding of locks, restraints, traps, observation cameras and any other device designed to keep you out of an area you are not supposed to be in. With a good Security you can override locked doors, unlock handcuffs, and predict when the next surveillance sweep is taking place in an enemy compound.

sleightOfHand.name: Sleight of Hand
sleightOfHand.description: Sleight of hand is the art of making small objects ‘disappear’, often into your pocket. It allows you to grab small items, no bigger than your hand, without anyone looking and place them anywhere you can reach. Unless you plan on becoming a stage magician this Skill is most commonly used by thieves to pinch stuff that doesn’t belong to them.

stealth.name: Stealth
stealth.description: Stealth covers both your ability to hide and to remain quiet. Sneaking around is a very useful Skill for spies and saboteurs, and indeed anyone who’d prefer to avoid combat.

survival.name: Survival
survival.description: This Skill covers the ability to survive in hostile natural environments. It is most useful on alien ‘earth-type’ worlds where it might be possible to scavenge for food and water, but at its most basic level it helps you find shelter, conserve your supplies and keep you alive long enough to be rescued. Those with a high Survival Skill might even be able to track people or animals through the wilderness.

sheet.cyberKarmaHint: Maximum cyber-only Karma (2 per Cyber enhancement)
sheet.adjustmentsHint: Use these for enhancements, cybernetics and other effects that change your maximums (e.g. Tough: +5 Endurance).
sheet.skillUsedHint: Used this adventure — improves by 1 at the end of the adventure
sheet.rollAttack: Attack: Fighting check vs Finesse 5 + target's Defence
sheet.equipmentComing: Arrives with the equipment item types.

escapeDeath.name: Escape Death
escapeDeath.description: Survive an attack that would have killed you or dropped your Endurance below 1. Your Karma points drop to zero.

sheet.clothingHint: Clothing and armour you have with you. Tick what you are wearing: worn clothing gives its Social Factor.
sheet.speedHint: Movement per turn: 10m, +2m per Quick Runner.

systemMaxBackgrounds.name: Maximum Background choices
systemMaxBackgrounds.hint: Specifies the maximum number of background choices. Default value is 4. 'Trained Pilot' is free and it is not included in the pool. 0 means unlimited choices

defaultDifficultyNumber.name: Default test difficulty number
defaultDifficultyNumber.hint: Specifies the default difficulty number for roll checks

allowToRerollAllTests.name: Allow to reroll all tests
allowToRerollAllTests.hint: Homerule - allows to reroll all tests using Karma point. Core Book rule allows to reroll only when there is a 1 on roll dice

socialFactorCap.name: Social Factor cap (house rule)
socialFactorCap.hint: Maximum positive Social Factor added to rolls. 0 = no cap, as in the Core Rules.

explosiveMode.name: Explosives: battle map
explosiveMode.hint: Grenades and missiles work differently with and without a map (Core Rules pp.58–60): the grenade difficulty, where a miss lands, and who is caught. "Ask" lets the attacker choose each time; cards without a choice offer both.

warning.karmaCapabilityLimit: Karma capability limit reached for rank '{rank}'
warning.pilotTrainedBuiltIn: Player characters already have Pilot Trained for free.
warning.weaponNotFound: Weapon "{name}" isn't in the Weapons compendium; add it by hand.

item.choicesHint: Some backgrounds (e.g. Army Trained) take two choices.
item.freeHint: Does not count towards the character's limit.
item.costAllHint: Spends the whole Karma pool and can't be used at 0 (Escape Death).
item.skillModsWeaponHint: Applied while the weapon is equipped (e.g. +10 Parry for a Neo-Samurai Sword).
item.skillModsArmourHint: Applied while the armour is worn (e.g. Riot Armour −20 Athletics).
item.boostHint: Offered on the attack card: an attack bonus while your attack misses, a defence bonus while an attack against you hits.
item.grantsHint: Added from the Enhancements compendium when this background is added to a character, and removed with it.
item.requiresHint: Any one of these backgrounds, separated by commas.
item.rollBonusesHint: "Always" bonuses are added to every check with that Skill; the others are offered as tick boxes in the check dialog (Medpacks are ticked for Stabilise and Treat wounds). A Skill score bonus counts only if it lifts your Skill bonus.
item.skillModsWornHint: Applied while worn (clothing) or installed (cybernetics), e.g. Cybernetic Eyes +5 Perception.

skillConfig.title: Skill
skillConfig.learningHint: Permanent improvements: independent learning at creation, rank-up D10s and +1 from each ticked adventure.
skillConfig.capBonusHint: Rank Skill Cap is {cap}. Natural Genius raises one skill's cap by 10.
skillConfig.modHint: Added to the score after the Skill Cap; the score can never exceed 100.

socialFactor.title: Social Factor
socialFactor.hint: Added to Bargain, Bluff, Charm and Diplomacy rolls (not to the Skill score). The GM can rule it doesn't apply to a particular roll.
socialFactor.wornHint: Social Factor of clothing and other items (e.g. Tailored Business Suit +1, wrist com −2). Worn armour is added automatically.
socialFactor.damagedHint: You lose any positive Social Factor from clothing once you take damage. Ticked automatically when Endurance drops; untick after changing clothes.
socialFactor.cosmeticsHint: Only one cosmetics bonus applies at a time. Refusing to use cosmetics is −1.
socialFactor.otherHint: Any other adjustment the GM allows.
socialFactor.cyborgHint: Non-discreet or revealed cybernetics: Social Factor is −3 and nothing else alters it.
socialFactor.confidentHint: No Social Factor penalties from equipment, armour or cybernetics.

endAdventure.title: End of Adventure
endAdventure.buttonHint: Ticked skills gain +1 (unless that would exceed the Skill Cap) and all ticks are cleared. Optionally restores Karma for the next adventure.
endAdventure.atCap: At Skill Cap — tick cleared, no improvement
endAdventure.ticksCleared: All skill ticks will be cleared.
endAdventure.restoreKarma: Restore all Karma for the next adventure ({value} / {max})

contest.opponentBonusHint: For opponents without the skill listed, e.g. their Perception or To Hit from the stat block.

ties.initiator: Ties: the acting character (opponent's roll sets the difficulty)

pairs.stealth: Core Rules p.267: the searcher's Perception check is the number your Stealth must pass.
pairs.charm: Core Rules p.33 (Seduce): Charm against the target's Insight check.
pairs.athletics: Core Rules p.61 (Grab/Escape): you must beat the opponent's Athletics; ties go to them.

contest.needsGM: A GM must be logged in to update this contest.

tiesShort.initiator: Ties go to the acting character

karma.useHint: Spend the Karma and post the effect to chat.
karma.usedHint: Already used this turn; you get it back at the start of your next turn.
karma.usedThisTurn: {name} has already been used this turn.
karma.restHint: Main rest (a full night's sleep): regain 1 Karma point.
karma.usedThisBattle: {name} has already been used this battle.
karma.usesLeft: Opponent capability — {left} of {max} uses left this battle

damage.title: Damage
damage.explosiveKnock: Everyone caught in the blast is knocked over, unless the GM rules otherwise.
damage.knock: A 10 on the damage dice: the target is knocked over.
damage.noKnockEnergy: A 10 was rolled, but Energy weapons have no concussive force: no knockdown.
damage.applySelectedHint: Select the tokens that were hit (e.g. everyone in the blast radius, or within 6m for divided fire).
damage.noneSelected: Select the tokens to apply the damage to first.
damage.escapeDeathHint: Spend all your Karma to avoid the attack that just dropped you below 1 Endurance.

bleed.odd: {name} rolls {roll}: loses {loss} Endurance, an odd number — stabilised.
bleed.even: {name} rolls {roll}: loses {loss} Endurance, an even number — still bleeding.
bleed.cauterised: {name} rolls {roll}: the Energy wound is cauterised — stabilised, no further damage.
bleed.cauterisedTen: {name} rolls a 10: the internal damage is too severe — loses {loss} Endurance and keeps bleeding.

damage.noMedic: Select the token of the character giving aid (or set your user character) first.
damage.deathAtHint: Below 0 Endurance a character bleeds out; at a negative score of half maximum Endurance they die.
damage.bleedOutHint: Lose a D10 Endurance: odd stabilises, even keeps bleeding. Rolled automatically at the start of the turn in combat.
damage.stabiliseHint: An ally's Medicine check (select their token): difficulty 8 if dropped by an Energy weapon, 10 otherwise.
damage.treatHint: Medicine check with a Medpack or proper kit, at most every six hours: heals the check's total. Select the medic's token to have someone else treat.
damage.disarm: Even number on the Fighting die: a weapon or item is knocked out of the target's hands (the GM picks where).
damage.freeKnock: It was a free attack: their turn ends.
damage.aimHint: Spend your turn aiming at one enemy for +5 To Hit next turn. Lost if you take damage, are attacked in close combat, or lose sight of them.

weapon.attackBonusHint: A rare weapon's bonus to the attacker's Skill score, used only when attacking with this weapon (never above 100).
weapon.damageHint: Damage is a roll formula (1d10, 3d10, 8). Burst adds damage for each point the attack beats the difficulty, up to the maximum.
weapon.reload: Reload (a fresh magazine; leftover rounds are lost)
weapon.equippedHint: In hand: its skill modifiers apply
weapon.rollHint: Roll an attack ({skill}). Shift-click to skip the dialog.
weapon.rollOpponent: Roll an attack with this weapon
weapon.reloadedNoSpare: {weapon} reloaded (no spare ammunition carried for it).

armour.hint: Absorbs damage of the listed types; every hit still does at least 1 damage, except Toxic. Hardened N: roll a D10, and on N or more the protection is doubled. Discreet armour worn under clothes has no Social Factor penalty.

combat.protectionHint: Armour absorbs damage of its types; every hit still does at least 1 damage, except Toxic. Hardened: on a D10 of that number or more the protection is doubled.
combat.karmaHint: Personal and Any Combat capabilities, for quick use in a fight.

opponent.fightingLine: Finesse 5, +{toHit} To Hit, Damage 1D10 halved (Fighting is To Hit −1 unless listed)
opponent.karmaHint: Opponents have no Karma points: each capability can be used once per battle.

attack.title: Attack: {weapon}
attack.noAmmo: {weapon} is out of ammo — reload first.
attack.noTarget: No target selected: enter the target's Defence below, or target a token first.
attack.squaresHint: Difficulty is 7 or the number of squares, whichever is greater.
attack.groundTargetHint: For explosives aimed at a patch of ground or a wall rather than at an enemy.
attack.coverHint: Behind boxes, a tree or other people. Ranged attacks only.
attack.defenceHint: Melee and Fighting attacks can be Dodged or Parried; the GM chooses for opponents.
attack.aimHint: Aimed at this enemy for a whole turn and kept the aim.
attack.knockedOverHint: Adds no skill bonus to the attack.
attack.divideFireHint: Hits everyone within 6m of the target (at least 8m away) on the same roll; damage is halved.
attack.adjustHint: Anything else the GM rules (e.g. darkness, smoke).
attack.cantEvade: The target can't evade: only the weapon's difficulty counts.
attack.divideFireNote: Divided fire: also checks everyone within 6m of the target; halve the damage.
attack.destroyCoverNote: If it missed only because of cover, the cover is destroyed (unless very tough).
attack.explosiveNote: Explosion: Fatal and Injury radii take their damage; everyone caught is knocked over unless the GM rules otherwise.
attack.boostHint: Spend the Karma and add this to the attack you just made.
attack.defenceBoostHint: {name}: spend the Karma and add this to your Defence against this attack.
attack.throwWithHint: With advantage: round a corner, down stairs, somewhere you can duck into cover. With disadvantage: bowled in an open fire-fight.
attack.freeHint: An adjacent enemy moved away or shot at point blank range. If this knocks them over, their turn ends.
attack.grabHint: Only someone roughly your size or smaller. On a hit, an opposed Athletics check (plus Strength damage bonuses) decides it.
attack.counterHint: You Parried and the attack missed: make an immediate Melee or Fighting attack (it doesn't use your next action).
attack.counterIntro: Counter-attack: the enemy can't counter this if it misses.
attack.counterMissNote: A missed counter-attack can't be countered (except with Riposte).
attack.riposteHint: Spend the Karma to counter-attack the counter-attack that just missed you.

background.chooseEnhancements: {name}: choose {count} Enhancement(s) from the Enhancements compendium.

hint.ambidextrous: Automated: the two-weapon penalty on attacks becomes −1, then 0.
hint.awareness: Automated: Initiative uses the better of your Tactics and Perception bonuses.
hint.confident: Automated: Social Factor ignores penalties from equipment, armour and cybernetics.
hint.dynamicKarma: Not automated: remember to pay only for the most expensive capability.
hint.hardToKill: Automated: death at minus maximum Endurance; twice, Escape Death costs at most 4 Karma.
hint.naturalGenius: Automated: +10 to the chosen Skill's Skill Cap (max 100).
hint.quickRunner: Automated: +2m Speed each time (up to three times).
hint.strong: Automated: +2 Fighting and Melee damage each time (max +10).
hint.tough: Automated: +5 maximum Endurance each time (up to 80).

creation.title: Character creation
creation.finishIncomplete: Only {done} of {total} steps are done. Finish creation anyway? (Endurance and Karma will be filled to their maximums and this checklist hidden.)
creation.overCap: Above the Skill Cap of {cap}: {skills}. Lower a background bonus or pick a different Skill.
creation.learningHint: Pick ten Skills to improve: +10 to the first, +9 to the second … +1 to the tenth. The number after each Skill is its score before these points; no Skill may go above {cap}.

hint.backgrounds: Four choices; two-choice backgrounds such as Army Trained use two. Pilot Trained is free and already on the sheet.
hint.openSkills: Self-Taught and University Graduate have skill lines for you to choose: open the background and pick the Skills.
hint.enhancements: Gene Mod Baby and Self-Taught let you choose Enhancements: drag them from the Enhancements compendium.
hint.karma: Pick three from the Karma Capabilities compendium. Escape Death is free and doesn't count.
hint.equipment: One or two Autopistols or Laser Pistols (two spare clips for Autopistols), Flight Suit, Magboots, Remlok, a hand-held or wrist com, 1000 credits; a knife, sword or sledgehammer with Melee Weapons 20+, a Fragmentation grenade with Grenade 20+. On the ship: a Spacesuit, a Medpack and a basic Spaceship Repair Kit.
hint.ship: Choose one of the eight starting ships, or build one with up to 100,000 credits (unspent credits are lost).
hint.finish: Finishing fills Endurance and Karma to their maximums and hides this checklist.
hint.partnerBackgrounds: Three choices for a partner; Pilot Trained isn't free but can be one of them.
hint.partnerEquipment: The same personal equipment as a character (pistol, Flight Suit, Magnetic Boots, Remlok, com, a melee weapon or grenade at 20+), but no ship.

creation.equipmentIntro: Adds the starting kit from the compendia and 1000 credits. You can't spend money until the game starts unless the GM says otherwise.
creation.partnerEquipmentIntro: Adds the personal starting kit from the compendia. Partners don't get a ship or its equipment.

gear.activeHint: In use: its Social Factor counts (a com on show, cosmetics applied, a gas mask on).
gear.hint: Bonuses apply while carried. Ammunition is used up when you reload a weapon whose name (or compendium group) contains the text above.

cybernetic.karmaHint: Cybernetics drain Karma permanently, from cybernetic Karma (Cybernetic Affinity) first. Upgrading a device you already have costs no Karma: set the new one's cost to 0.
cybernetic.karmaSummary: Karma drained: {spent} from your Karma maximum, {fromCyber} from cybernetic Karma.
cybernetic.cyborgNote: Cybernetics show (or are revealed): Social Factor is fixed at −3.

clothing.hint: Worn clothing gives its Social Factor (positive values are lost once you take damage) and its Skill modifiers.

hint.mapped: D10 for the direction from the target square (1–8 clockwise from the square above it; 9–10 overshoots along the line of fire), then D10 squares.
hint.mapless: Roll on the Grenade or Missile Miss Table.
hint.caught: If the GM is unsure how many people are in the blast: roll a D10 and halve it.

scatter.mappedResult: Scatter {roll}: {direction}, {squares} squares ({metres}m) from the target square. It stops at a wall or solid obstacle, then explodes.
scatter.mappedOvershoot: Scatter {roll}: overshoots — it carries on {squares} squares ({metres}m) past the target square along the line from you, stopping at a wall or solid obstacle, then explodes.

grenade.short: Rubbish throw! It slips from your grasp and rolls only {metres} metres forward before exploding.
grenade.whoosh: Whoosh! Complete miss: it explodes where it injures no one (the GM may rule it damages equipment).
grenade.long: Too long! It lands {metres} metres beyond the target point, or against the back wall.
grenade.random: What the…? It bounces off walls and ceilings and lands at the feet of a random person, chosen by the GM.

missile.whoosh: Whoosh! Complete miss: it explodes where it injures no one (the GM may rule it damages equipment).
missile.long: Too long! It lands {metres} metres beyond the target point, or against the back wall.
missile.short: Ooops! It lands {metres} metres short of the target point, possibly with you in the blast.

scatter.caughtResult: Caught in the blast: D10 {roll}, halved — {people} (the GM decides who is in the fatal or injury radius).

modeNote.mapless: Explosives without a map: the GM decides who is in each radius.

grab.resolveHint: Both roll Athletics plus Strength damage bonuses (opponents may use To Hit); you must beat the target.
grab.success: grabbed! Both have Dodge 0 and can't Parry; the target can only try to escape.
grab.escapeHint: Your action: Athletics (+ Strength) against the grabber's; you must exceed it.
grab.escaped: Escaped! You can still move, and the grabber gets no free attack.

stim.title: Stim injector
stim.injectHint: Inject a carried Combat Stim (needs a syringe or injector). Unconscious characters wake, knocked over.
stim.endsHint: After about an hour. At 0 Endurance or less you fall unconscious.
stim.noInjector: You need a syringe or Stim injector to apply it.
stim.injected: {injector}: rolled {roll} (needed {chance} or less) — {drug} injected; {name} stays conscious.
stim.failed: {injector}: rolled {roll} (needed {chance} or less) — no injection; it tries again at the end of each of {name}'s turns.
stim.overload: {injector}: rolled 100 — the stimulant overloads {name}'s heart. Dead.

rankUp.title: Rank up: {rank}
rankUp.banner: New rank reached: {rank} (Skill Cap {cap}). Apply the rank-up to improve ten Skills and choose a Karma Capability or Enhancement.
rankUp.more: ({count} ranks to apply, one at a time.)
rankUp.choiceEnhancement: A new Enhancement (instead of a Karma Capability)
rankUp.skillsHint: Choose ten different Skills; each gains a D10, but none can go above the new Skill Cap ({cap}). The number shown is the current score.
rankUp.pickTen: Choose {count} Skills (fewer only if no other Skill has room under the cap).
rankUp.pickKarma: {name}: drag a new Karma Capability from the compendium onto the sheet.
rankUp.pickEnhancement: {name}: drag a new Enhancement from the compendium onto the sheet.
rankUp.partnerNote: A partner rolls ten Skills and gains 5 Endurance, but no Karma point, Karma Capability or Enhancement.
rankUp.partnerChoice: No new Karma Capability or Enhancement (partner)

partner.tooDeep: The third partner in a chain can't have a partner of their own (they would start off dead).
partner.noKarmaItems: Partners have no Karma Capabilities of their own: they use their host's.
partner.backgroundLimit: Partners have {limit} background choices (Pilot Trained uses one).
partner.noHost: {name} has no host character to draw Karma from.
partner.hostRefuses: {host} doesn't let their partner spend their Karma.
partner.visibleCybernetics: {name} has visible cybernetics and can no longer use {host}'s Karma.
partner.notHostOwner: You need permission on {host} to spend their Karma.
partner.confirmUnknown: Can {name} see {host}, within {range}m? (Their tokens aren't both on this scene.)
partner.confirmFar: {name} is {distance}m from {host} — more than {range}m. Use the Karma anyway (e.g. the GM allows it)?
partner.virtualKarma: Cybernetics: {cost} of {total} virtual Karma (the host's total)
partner.rankHint: A partner's rank follows the host's Rank Points.
partner.ranksUp: {name} (a partner) has a rank-up to apply.
partner.allowKarma: My partner may spend my Karma
partner.allowKarmaHint: A partner who can see you within 30m can use your Karma Capabilities, paid from your Karma (Core Rules p.27).
partner.depth3: (third in the chain: Endurance −15; can't have a partner)

craft.weaponHint: Burst weapons add 5 damage for each point the attack beats the target's Defence, up to the maximum. Kinetic weapons typically add +5 against Hull, energy weapons +5 against Shields; missiles list lower damage against Shields.

vehicle.pilotHint: Drag a character or opponent onto the sheet, or choose one here. Their Vehicle Piloting gives Defence and Pursuit, Tactics gives Initiative, and Vehicle Weapons fires the fixed and gimballed weapons.
vehicle.defenceHint: Agility + the pilot's Vehicle Piloting bonus + the Speed Table bonus. 0 when stationary.
vehicle.pursuitHint: Current Speed + half the pilot's Vehicle Piloting bonus (rounded down).
vehicle.shieldsDownHint: Knocked-out shields charge up by their recharge each turn and work again once back to half their maximum.
vehicle.zoneFromMap: (from the token's position on the combat map)
vehicle.setSpeedHint: Set the current speed (click again to stop)
vehicle.noTarget: No vehicle targeted: type the target's Defence.
vehicle.targetDefenceHint: 0 if the target is stationary or sniping.
vehicle.naturalTen: Natural 10: against a spaceship this would also hit a component (vehicles take no critical hits).
vehicle.selectVehicles: Select the vehicle tokens to damage first.
